utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case IT-08-91-T, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Good morning to everyone. May we have the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Joanna Korner assisted by Crispian Smith, Case Manager, for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Slobodan Zecevic, Slobodan Cvijetic, and Eugene O'Sullivan appearing for Stanisic Defence this morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. For Zupljanin Defence, Igor Pantelic and Dragan Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Before we revert to closed session, there was an issue that came up just at the adjournment yesterday. I'm wondering whether it's something on which a ruling has to be made before we -- before we go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. Your Honours. Can I tell Your Honours, I can say this in open session. I spoke to the witness yesterday after we adjourned. There was a misunderstanding. What he would like to have in front of him is the document on which his evidence really, as far as the Prosecution is concerned, is based. He had obviously been given a tour of the court by VWS who told him the document would come up on the screen, and what he actually wanted -- he wants to have a hard copy of the document in front of him, and that -- I gave him a copy --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: The document, is that his statement?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's the document that I asked Your Honours to read. It's an exhibit in this case, exactly. That one. He says if he was going be asked question about it he would prefer to have a hard copy. I gave him that yesterday. I had an unmarked copy which he took with him. And the second matter that he wanted clarified, he wants it made absolutely clear that is he not attending voluntarily, and I assured him that will be made clear at the beginning of his evidence. And can I say I gave that explanation to both of my friends yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. So we go into closed session. Sorry, something, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yeah, it's a small matter, Your Honours, but I would just like to make the record straight in respect to the -- to our conversation and exchanges yesterday about the adjudicated facts. Well, Your Honours, there has been the first and the second motion which dealt with the adjudicated facts between number 1 and 983, and it has been decided on the 14th of December, 2007. In that respect, the -- the Stanisic Defence agreed to 84 of these facts. Now, from 25th of January, 2008, until the 21st of August, 2009 there were additional three motions for adjudicated facts, and the -- the last, the fifth motion, from 21st August, 2009, ended with the number 1442 adjudicated facts, and this Trial Chamber decided on April 1st, 2010. Now, there has been a suggestion yesterday that there was -- there was an offer made to the -- to the Defence in the course of the pre-trial or immediately before the start of the trial on adjudicated facts, an offer, and an invitation to agree to some of these facts, but that is -- we -- we exchanged the -- the mails and we consulted with each other, and it is not a fact. It has -- it hasn't been offered to the Defence in the pre-trial phase. Only in December -- before the December 2007 motion -- decision, and on that, we agreed to 84 facts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I'm not sure of whose offer you're talking.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Because I recall when I was the Pre-Trial Judge that I invited the parties, collectively, to get together and seek agreement on as many of the proposed adjudicated facts as possible. And although I didn't check it, I would be inclined to believe that the Defence counsels' were, in particular, invited to come forward with a proposal as to how many of the adjudicated facts you could actually agree to among the adjudicated facts that had been proposed by the time I was the Pre-Trial Judge. And I think - but I cannot recall for sure - but I think that the response both by you and by Mr. Pantelic was that the general position was that you objected to all of them. But I may be wrong. But -- but please correct me if I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: With all due respect, Your Honours, I don't think you're wrong. I just think that the issue that we were talking about were the crime base. That was the issue that Your Honour invited us to find an agreement with the -- with the Prosecution. And we were talking about the -- the -- the -- the crime base witnesses, in order, if we can -- if we can stipulate to some of the facts and some of the crime base which our friends from the Prosecutors are alleging. And I don't think that we -- that we -- that we discussed any other adjudicated fact or -- or -- or -- or have been offered by the Prosecution and -- or -- or invited to -- to accept some of the adjudicated facts. Because when you -- when your -- when Your Honour yesterday pointed out the -- the ethnic composition according to the census of 1991, absolutely, we are not going to challenge that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Then say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well ... well, I believe, Your Honours, the parties should -- should communicate on that, and it is our position that -- that we should -- we should sit down with -- with our friends from the Prosecution and -- yeah. I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. I think enough has been said about this matter. Let's just get on with --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, can I just. Your Honours, what Your Honours are referring to, and I -- on the 24th of August, before that, and as Mr. Zecevic says, Your Honours invited us to try and agree the crime base. We were asked to identify the perpetrators by the Defence. We did so as far as we were able. We sent the Defence a list of the crimes which formed the crime base in this indictment with the identified perpetrators and asked for their agreement. We got a refusal from the Defence for Zupljanin to agree this unless we dropped JCE, so we never took the matter any further, and, indeed, I wrote a letter. And you were told about it in the Status Conference on the 24th of August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And we explained that to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Right. I think we should cut it here and take it up at a later point. Let's get on with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 14th day of May, 2010, at 9.00 a.m. 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 5.31 p.m.,
